subject: Biology
title: The Evolution of Aging
description: A fast breakdown of The Evolution of Aging for builders.

hook.text: Greenland sharks live over 400 years. Mayflies live one day. Why does lifespan vary so dramatically?

buildup.text: Natural selection is strongest in young, reproductive individuals and weakens with age.

discovery.text: Harmful genes that act late in life aren't removed by selection—nobody reproduced that late to be affected.

twist.text: Some organisms don't age. Hydra and certain jellyfish show negligible senescence—they can theoretically live forever.

climax.text: Understanding why aging evolved could lead to interventions that extend healthy human lifespan.

punchline.text: Aging isn't a design flaw. It's a priority trade-off.

quiz.question: Why do harmful late-acting genes persist in populations?
options: Natural selection is too weak at old ages to remove them
They are beneficial early in life only
They mutated too recently to be eliminated

details.summary: Aging evolves because natural selection's power weakens after organisms begin reproducing. Genes that cause harm late in life face weak selection against them, especially if they provide benefits early. This explains why all complex organisms deteriorate with age despite evolution's power.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding why aging evolves could help extend healthy lifespan. It explains why no species has evolved immortality and why aging-related diseases are universal. Evolutionary medicine suggests novel approaches to age-related diseases.
takeaways: Natural selection weakens for effects that occur after peak reproduction
Antagonistic pleiotropy means genes beneficial early can cause harm late
Some species like hydra and certain tortoises show negligible senescence

faq.question: Why haven't organisms evolved to live forever?
faq.answer: Natural selection cares about reproduction, not longevity. Once an organism has reproduced, genes affecting later life face weaker selection. Investing resources in maintenance versus reproduction involves tradeoffs, and evolution consistently favors reproduction.

faq.question: Do any animals not age?
faq.answer: Some species show negligible senescence, meaning they do not measurably deteriorate with age. Hydra, some tortoises, rockfish, and naked mole rats age very slowly. They still die from disease, predation, or accident, but their aging rate is remarkably low.
